claim_being_audited: The model can be certified for launch on the current record because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, general launch checks passed, and the remaining API migration-guidance gap is acceptable if treated as an explicit unknown and disclosed in the model card and audit record.

concern_ledger.concern: No admissible evidence shows the required disclosure of the API migration-guidance evaluation gap has been made in the final model card or audit record.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Final model card and audit record showing the gap is explicitly disclosed as unknown coverage, or approved risk-acceptance documentation.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: Policy requires disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance for material limitations and evaluation gaps in named deployment contexts before clean certification.

concern_ledger.concern: The draft model card currently overstates migration coverage by saying there are no known developer-support migration limitations because no completed test failed.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Revised final model card language removing the 'no known limitations' claim and replacing it with an explicit unknown-coverage disclosure, or completed eval results demonstrating the claim is accurate.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: That statement conflicts with the admissible evidence that the relevant evals are missing and should be treated as unknown rather than passed, creating a material disclosure defect.

concern_ledger.concern: There is no admissible evidence of completed API migration-guidance evals or approved risk acceptance for that named context.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Completed migration-guidance eval results, or approved risk-acceptance documentation explicitly covering that context.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: Without either completed coverage or accepted residual risk, the certification predicate remains unresolved under the stated policy.

decision_criteria: Certification is supportable only if named deployment-context evaluation gaps are either resolved, explicitly disclosed in the model card and audit record, or covered by approved risk acceptance.
Aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and passing general support/latency/rollback checks support readiness but do not substitute for missing named-context coverage.
A draft model card that states no known migration limitations does not satisfy the disclosure requirement when admissible evidence says the relevant evals are still missing.
evidence_requests: Final model card text showing the API migration-guidance evaluation gap is disclosed as unknown coverage for a named deployment context.
Final audit record or certification memo showing the same gap disclosure before certification.
If disclosure will not be made, approved risk-acceptance evidence covering the named deployment context.
If available, completed migration-guidance eval results closing the gap.
specific_concerns: The admissible record supports launch readiness in aggregate, but it also shows a named deployment context, API migration guidance, lacks completed evaluation coverage.
The policy requires material limitations and evaluation gaps for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The current draft model card appears inconsistent with that requirement because it says there are no known migration limitations, while QA says the missing evals are unknown rather than passed.
There is no admissible evidence that the model card and audit record have already been corrected to disclose the gap, and no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance.
unsupported_claims: Any claim that the current packet already supports clean certification without further disclosure of the migration-guidance gap.
Any claim that API migration guidance effectively passed because no completed test failed.
Any claim that the required model-card disclosure or approved risk acceptance already exists in the admissible record.
